sections.skill: Distinguish sales tax from income tax and handle collected tax

questions.prompt: Who pays sales tax in the end?

choices.text: Nobody; it is optional for every sale
The customer, collected by the business
The business, out of its own profit
The supplier, before the item is shipped

questions.correct_answer: The customer, collected by the business
questions.intro: SALES TAX is charged to customers on certain sales; the business collects it and sends it to the state or local government. It is not the business's money. Rules vary: some states have no general sales tax, and some items or services may be exempt. A business may need a permit or account before collecting. INCOME TAX is a tax on the business's profit (for many small businesses, reported on the owner's return). Keep collected sales tax separate so it is not spent by accident.

questions.prompt: The coach's 5 dollars is like what?

choices.text: The business's own profit for the day

questions.intro: Imagine a friend gives you 5 dollars to pass to the coach. That money is in your pocket, but it is not yours. Sales tax is like that: customers give it to you to pass to the government. Income tax is different: it is a tax on what you yourself earned as profit. Mixing the coach's 5 dollars with your own money can lead to spending it by mistake.
